summary:
We have built HabiTrack, an offline-first clinical intelligence console and habitat telemetry platform to protect astronaut health during deep-space and long-duration spaceflight missions.
In isolated space environments, subtle habitat fluctuations often occur along with physiological changes, but telemetry is usually fragmented and slowed by the latencies of interplanetary communication. HabiTrack solves this problem by fusing authentic NASA archive cabin environment telemetry (CO2, temperature, pressure, radiation), astronaut biometrics, and real-world smart watch health exports. Using individualized 7-day circadian baselines, the platform automatically detects clinical discordance (e.g. compensatory tachycardia plus localized hypercapnia) as dictated by official NASA standards and ISS flight rules.
This solution is vital because human missions to the Moon and Mars cannot depend on instant Earth ground control. HabiTrack is built on a 100% client-side TypeScript architecture with an offline-capable dual AI assistant that enables crew members and flight surgeons to independently detect health anomalies early, make evidence-based medical decisions, and maintain mission resilience even in complete communication blackouts.
details:
What does it do?

HabiTrack is an offline-first habitat telemetry and clinical intelligence platform. It synchronizes authentic ISS environmental data (CO₂, temperature, pressure, radiation) with astronaut physiological vitals, evaluating health against individual 7-day circadian baselines rather than static population averages. It automatically correlates habitat anomalies with vital signs, alerts crews under official NASA flight rules (e.g., FR-ECLSS), and offers tailored interfaces for both Astronauts and Flight Surgeons.

• How does it work?

Local Data Processing: Background Web Workers decompress and parse multi-megabyte smart watch / Apple Health export ZIPs on-device, storing normalized records in browser IndexedDB with zero cloud uploads.

Clinical Correlation: An integrated rule engine evaluates vital deviations against authentic NASA ISS telemetry (Expedition 41/72, Rodent Research-1).

Dual-Mode AI: Uses Google Gemini RAG when online with Earth, and seamlessly switches to an embedded offline engine (Ollama/local logic) during simulated deep-space communication blackouts.

• What benefits does it have?

Early Detection: Identifies environmental-physiological strain (like hypercapnic tachycardia) before acute clinical emergencies occur.

100% Offline Autonomy: Operates entirely in-browser with zero external servers, ideal for communication-delayed lunar and Martian missions.

Complete Privacy: Biometric data never leaves the astronaut's device.

• What do we hope to achieve?

We aim to transition astronaut care from reactive monitoring to proactive, autonomous protection. Future milestones include live BLE smartwatch streaming, human-in-the-loop autonomous ECLSS life-support control (auto-adjusting ventilation with crew confirmation), and surface EVA monitoring for Moon and Mars exploration.

• Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

Languages & UI: TypeScript, React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS.

Processing & Storage: Web Workers (multi-threading), fflate (streaming decompression), IndexedDB, LocalStorage.

Visualization & PDF: Plotly.js, Lucide Icons, jsPDF.

AI & Knowledge: Google Gemini API, Local Ollama fallback, NASA Human Research Roadmap (HRR) RAG corpus.

NASA Standards & Data: NASA Environmental Data Application (EDA) ISS telemetry, NASA-STD-3001, NASA-HRP Evidence Books, and ISS Flight Rules.
